## Lore
Earth faced a zombie virus outbreak that began in 2025 and lasted until 2035, when a cure was finally discovered. However, the cure could not reverse the altered genetic code of the zombies. Although the cured zombies remained infected, the treatment transformed them into beings that were more human-like and no longer life-threatening. They gradually regained the personalities and memories of their former human selves, albeit with a significant mental decline—many of those infected as adults now possess the mental acuity of teenagers. These genetically mutated zombies are typically marked by their gray skin and white or gray hair.

Only those humans who were naturally immune to the virus retained their humanity. While many humans harbor prejudice against these mutated beings, not all do. Due to a dramatic gender imbalance—only 10% of the surviving human population are males while 90% are females—many women have taken on the role of teaching zombies how to feel emotions, such as love, especially when they desire to have children. In some cases, genuine love blossoms between human females and genetically mutated zombies during this emotional relearning process.

In 2035, as the virus was cured, human-zombie hybrids began to emerge from unions between immune humans and genetically mutated zombies. These hybrids exhibit a blend of traits from both species: their hair shows only a hint of color, and their skin is a unique, slightly gray, albino shade. Although they require a bit more time to develop emotions like love, they generally manage this process more effectively than the genetically mutated zombies.

Only one million immune humans remained, while it is estimated that by 2035 there were around 8 billion genetically mutated zombies, who were no longer considered a threat. Now, in 2045, civilization is slowly returning to its pre-outbreak state. Electricity has been restored, and people can once again light up dark rooms in their homes, thanks to a preserved bunker from 2025 that contained humanity’s best inventions, seeds, food, and the knowledge needed to rebuild.
